# September 23, 2026 · `EL-RUN-2026-09-23-NOON-LINCOLN-R1`

**Counts:** 0 new · 1 changed · 0 excluded · 1 held  
**Visible pipeline:** 30 distinct advertised offerings  
**Verdict:** Keep Benson primary and the existing backups. Retain Lincoln Industrial Park as an unpaid research lead; promote none.  
**Delivery:** **SITE NOT UPDATED — MANUAL_INGESTION_REQUIRED.** No outreach, reminder, offer, negotiation, application, account, signature, spend, or website change occurred.

| New parcels | Work completed this run |

## Monetization card — `NC-LINCOLN-INDUSTRIAL-PARK-2PARCEL-v1.1`

- **Buyer/workload/payer:** Unvalidated data-center developer, operator, or funded sponsor. Workload, first/ultimate MW, ramp, latency endpoints, procurement authority, budget, acceptance standard, and decision maker are all **UNKNOWN**.
- **Potential scarce deliverable:** A seller-authorized two-parcel package that reconciles the offered boundary and acreage, proves joint disposition authority, produces the referenced Duke Site Readiness Report with issuer/reliance rights, and then—only if warranted—adds official use, water, access, environmental, power-study, and diverse-fiber evidence.
- **Buyer alternative:** Expand an existing campus, lease colocation, wait, or buy a site already carrying completed parcelization and transferable utility evidence.
- **Why it might pay:** Only if the report and later issuer evidence materially shorten a buyer's site-selection or interconnection path. No payer has confirmed this premise.
- **Next acceptance milestone:** Seller confirms the exact two offered parcels and all authorized signers, reconciles acreage, and supplies the complete Site Readiness Report plus ROW, title/access, creek/flood, water/sewer, power, and fiber records.
- **Control/reliance:** No control. Title, access, assignment, novation, utility/report reliance, sharing rights, change-control, liability release, and evidence transferability remain **UNKNOWN**.
- **Payment mechanism/date:** Option assignment, sponsor-funded origination, seller-supported evidence bridge, or scoped paid work are hypotheses only. There is no signed scope, commitment, invoice, acceptance, collection date, or realized profit.
- **Cheapest falsifier:** One founder-approved seller-document request to John Tate. Cost $0; no buyer, funding, capacity, control, or exclusivity representation.

## Material correction — exact parcel and acreage reconciliation

The live offer remains $2,700,000. The first-party broker page simultaneously says “over 92 acres” and lists 88.95 acres. A broker video description states 92.5484 acres. The official Lincoln County parcel service returns two vacant Industrial Park Road records whose mapped acreage sums to 88.947 acres—matching the headline—but whose tax acreage sums to 97.704 acres.

| Broker video description | Exact source basis not published | **92.5484** | $29,174 |

Sources: [first-party listing](https://www.haydenoutdoors.com/land-for-sale/lincolnton-industrial-park-acreage/), [LandSearch listing](https://www.landsearch.com/properties/industrial-park-rd-lincolnton-nc-28092/4875563), [official GIS page](https://www.lincolncountync.gov/289/GIS), and [official parcel-layer schema](https://arcgisserver.lincolncountync.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Server_TaxParcelViewerSP_App/MapServer/0). **Inference, not fact:** these two GIS records are likely the marketed pair because both are vacant Industrial Park Road parcels, the listing says the land lies on both sides of the road, and their mapped acreage rounds to the headline. Seller confirmation, deeds, survey, current title, and joint authority are still required. The two different assessor-listed owners create an assemblage/authority risk; they do not prove that either owner authorized a combined sale.

The listing point did not intersect the official Lincolnton city-limits layer, and both parcel records carry district `NORTH 321`. The marketing claim that city water and sewer are available therefore remains an extension/service claim—not a jurisdiction or capacity determination.

- **Corrected conservative 52-factor research screen:** **32/100**; confidence **64/100**; bounded **27–50**.

Duke describes its program as identifying and assessing potential industrial sites; the report itself was not found publicly. [Duke Site Readiness program](https://www.duke-energy.com/partner-with-us/economic-development/site-readiness-program) · [Duke program explanation](https://news.duke-energy.com/releases/duke-energy-helps-communities-across-north-carolina-prepare-sites-to-bring-local-investment-jobs)

Lincoln County states that Stage 2 mandatory water conservation has applied since May 1, 2026, targeting a 5%–10% reduction and restricting certain non-recycled water-cooled equipment. This applies to the county water system; the exact serving water authority and parcel capacity remain unresolved. [Official drought notice](https://www.lincolncountync.gov/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=1873) · [Official drought page](https://www.lincolncountync.gov/Drought)

No public carrier document identifies a fiber provider or route at either candidate parcel. Broadband availability or a single nearby line would not establish route diversity, capacity, latency, construction cost, SLA, or buyer acceptability.

## Full 34-topic desktop-first status

## M1–M4 and strongest counter-case

- **M2 — UNKNOWN:** No locally relevant option, acquisition, paid study, cost-recovery agreement, procurement, utility commitment, or development commitment by a funded data-center actor was found.

**Strongest counter-case:** the Site Readiness work may be generic, stale, non-reliance industrial planning. A divided two-owner assemblage, power ROW, creek/flood constraints, outside-city water/sewer ambiguity, and Stage 2 drought may materially reduce contiguous buildable area. A buyer can select an established campus or a site with transferable utility and carrier evidence.

Thirty-day test: obtain or fail to obtain the seller's existing documents. Ninety-day utility or carrier work remains blocked by exact scope, authority, report review, and separate approval. At 180 days, no named funded takeout means no paid control.

## Internal sample option business draft — not an offer

Only after documentary reconciliation, seller would grant a 90-day diligence option over the exact deeded parcels confirmed as the offering—currently hypothesized as PIN `3634052499` / parcel `21501` and PIN `3634064802` / parcel `58944`. 2. Store tax, mapped, surveyed, and marketed acreage as separate fields; never normalize them silently.

### Parcel-specific sample option business draft — INTERNAL / counsel review required

For each stable ID, the property schedule is the linked address, advertised gross acres and dated ask shown above. This is a business-points sample, not an offer and not authority to negotiate:

1. **Property/exhibit:** exact legal parcel(s), parent/portion status, survey-grade exhibit and every access/utility/rail/road easement; no description-by-map-pin.
2. **Price:** dated public ask is reference only; contract price and credits are `UNKNOWN / NOT PROPOSED`.

- Quarantined a pending Webster County 84-acre result; pending status is not currently available control.
- Deduplicated repeated Davis Ranch and other Land Network syndications; one underlying offering is counted once despite multiple portals.
- Excluded small residential lots returned by IQLand and the Prineville→Port Charlotte locality-parser failure.
- Excluded “utilities available,” existing wells, broadband labels, highway frontage and utility-territory proxies from protected power/fiber fields.
- County/APN, owner, serving utility and carrier contacts remain unresolved for most rows; this is a HOLD condition, not evidence of incapacity.

## Verdict and source/gate crosswalk

**Verdict: KEEP BENSON PRIMARY; ADMIT 20 VISIBLE UNPAID RESEARCH LEADS; PROMOTE NONE.** The correction expands discovery but does not relax G1/G2/G3 or the approval firewall. The strongest counter-case is that this page-one intake is dominated by farm/recreational land with missing parcel identity and no buyer-accepted utility/fiber evidence; even the best industrial-marketed tract may be overpriced land whose power path is infeasible.

- **Listing/source → G1:** live Land.com/Whitetail pages support dated asks and advertised gross acres only; assessor/title/authority remain unproven.
- **Seller infrastructure claim → G2:** preserved as seller claim; cannot establish serving utility, load delivery, energy supply, fiber diversity, water rights or engineering feasibility.
- **Atlas state score → market research:** rotates effort only; cannot offset a hard parcel, utility, legal, environmental or buyer failure.
- **Authoritative learning resource:** [Webster Electric Cooperative’s official site and line-extension notice](https://www.websterec.com/) illustrates that a general utility contact or line-extension policy is not parcel-specific service, capacity, schedule, tariff, credit or transferability evidence.

**Next decision:** approve/reject the three internal calls above, with `BENSON-R01-v2` still first in the primary queue. **Authorized spend/contact today: $0 / none.**

### Workflow improvements

1. Store `listing_headline_price`, `listing_body_price`, `syndicated_price`, `gross_acres`, `described_acres` and `legal_acres` separately; never overwrite contradictions.
2. Add a required discovery cursor and parser-quality field so page-one coverage and locality failures are visible.
3. Batch seller-document calls by verified broker contact, while keeping utility calls blocked until exact parcel and written seller authority exist.
